correctness.rationale: An exact finite-state induction covers every column length, not just a search window. Each of the \(27^2\) ordered column-pair states has its exact least prefix weight and exact tied multiplicity computed from the literal neighborhood equation. The standalone verifier checks the equality \(D_{14}=\operatorname{shift}_1(D_{13})\) on every pair state (306 reachable, all others impossible) and checks all base minima for lengths 4 through 14. Shift commutes with the transition, proving this identity for all later lengths; six explicit 3-periodic labelings attain the optimum at every length, exhausting the exact tie count. Independent vertex-by-vertex exhaustive checks confirm the length-4, length-5, length-6 cases. The graph is \(K_3\square P_n\), \(n\ge4\), and labels are 0,1,2; end columns use zero boundary vectors.

value.rationale: The previously studied perfect Italian domination number for Cartesian products includes exact two-row strips and clique-clique products, making a triangular strip a natural unresolved adjacent family. Here an exact value for all lengths is strengthened by a rigid classification: just six functions for arbitrarily large graphs, all 0/1-valued and generated by one global row permutation of a periodic template. This explains and enumerates every extremal solution, not merely an easy construction or a small numerical improvement.
